items.title: PostToolUse WHILE_BUSY drain trailer causes redundant re-acknowledgments
items.probe: PostToolUse hook injects 'USER MESSAGE(S) RECEIVED WHILE BUSY' via inbox.drain(). The drain block is attached as a system-reminder to the originating tool result and PERSISTS across later turns. Once acknowledged, the reminder text doesn't disappear — when a later turn re-reads that tool result, agent sees the same 'Pause current task to acknowledge' prompt and re-acknowledges. Observed 2026-05-20 during remember-md port arc: Turn N said 'Got it — direct inline execution. Starting Phase 1...'; Turn N+1 said 'Acknowledged — already pivoted to inline execution. Continuing.' — duplicate.
items.verify: Fix landed in commit 3bb0d63: rewrote the drain trailer to explicitly say 'If your immediately prior assistant turn already addressed these, continue silently — do NOT re-acknowledge.' Hard signal 'do NOT re-acknowledge' + actionable prior-turn check phrase. Paired test test_drain_trailer_discourages_redundant_ack asserts both phrases. 11/11 inbox tests pass.

items.title: Semantic auto-skill-routing — replace explicit Skill tool calls with intent-detected dispatch
items.probe: Today the agent loads skills via the Skill tool (e.g. Skill(onion-ddd-workflow)). The kaizen plugin already has the infrastructure for semantic routing — intent_routing.yaml + route_intent.py + brain semantic search + UserPromptSubmit hook + dxm trace. Instead of explicit skill calls, use these existing systems to AUTO-detect which skill(s) should apply based on the semantic content of the user's prompt + the file deltas + the trace stream. The agent never has to manually load — the right skill activates based on context. Bypass knob: KAIZEN_SEMANTIC_ROUTING_DISABLE=1.
items.verify: Test fixture: user prompt 'refactor this onion thing' → semantic-routing returns Skill(onion-ddd-workflow) + Skill(refactor) without explicit Skill tool call. Test prompt 'fix bug in X' → returns Skill(systematic-debugging) + Skill(test-driven-development). Test prompt with no semantic match → no skills auto-loaded (silent). Backend: extend route_intent.py to also emit a skill-match list given the prompt's intent, fed by the intent_routing.yaml -> skill mapping.

items.title: Semantic learning-detector — content-based trigger for self-improving review
items.probe: Today stop_self_improving_review.py fires the curation nudge every N Stops (default 5) — a time/counter trigger, not a content trigger. Result: nudges fire even when there are no learnings to extract; or stay quiet when a rich session would have benefited from immediate review. Wanted: a checker that scans recent session jsonl + auto-memory + dxm trace for learning candidates (pattern recurrence ≥2 sessions, novel decisions captured, repeated corrections, gold-marked patterns) and triggers the review ONLY when content warrants it. Re-use existing primitives: brain_audit's discovery output, intent_routing.yaml for semantic detection, dxm trace events, learning_log.py if it exists.
items.verify: Test fixture: a session jsonl with 0 learning candidates → checker returns no-trigger. A session jsonl with 3+ matched patterns → checker emits a Stop hookSpecificOutput nudging /kaizen:self-improving review. Plus a CLI: kaizen-learning-detector scan [--since N_sessions] [--threshold N_candidates].

items.title: Sweep 110 .py shims at skills/workflow/scripts/ (high-risk .py subset of BK-065)
items.probe: After f6b36e9 the .sh subset of BK-065 is done. 110 .py MIGRATION BRIDGE shims remain at skills/workflow/scripts/. Earlier bulk-delete attempt this arc went 4 fail → 70 fail because consumers use sys.path.insert(0, '<skills/workflow/scripts>') + bare 'import <name>' chains. Each shim forwards via importlib.spec_from_file_location + sys.modules alias, so deleting the shim breaks the consumer's import even when canonical exists.

Or: write a single 'shim-redirector' at skills/workflow/scripts/__init__.py that programmatically aliases sys.modules['<name>'] for every legacy name once and for all, then drop the per-file shims. Test each batch of ~10 shims; revert any that break suite.
